title: WellaPath Nigeria facilities artifact — schema 2.0 (candidate)
description:
Schema for the nationwide facilities candidate. Additive over schema 1.0: every field facilities 1.1 emitted is still present under the same name and type, so the Mobile consumer's field access is unchanged. Two of those fields — type and emergency_capable — are null on every record because this source evidences neither; that is a behavioural change for the consumer even though the shape is unchanged, and it is the reason the artifact version is 2.0 rather than 1.2.

Coordinate policy (Step 2): latitude and longitude are non-null on every record. A source row without a usable pair is quarantined with its reason, never emitted with nulls and never given a substitute point. Exact duplicates (same name, state, LGA and coordinates) are collapsed to one survivor by a documented, total rule recorded in _metadata.deduplication; no values are merged.

Absence convention, applied throughout: null means NOT PROVIDED (the source field was blank or a placeholder token). The literal string "unknown" means the source explicitly recorded Unknown, which is a different statement. No absent value is ever represented as false, zero or an invented value.

release_status.description: Pinned. A candidate becomes something else only through a recorded approval, never through regenerating it. This is the lifecycle field every artifact in the repository carries.

publication_status.description: Pinned to the same constant as release_status. The two names describe one fact; pinning both means neither can drift.

may_publish.description: Pinned false. Licence for this source is not established, which is a blocking gate independent of any technical readiness.

states_absent.description: States with no row in the source at all. Present and non-empty for this candidate; the artifact states its own coverage gap rather than leaving a reader to discover it.

states_with_no_emitted_records.description: States that have rows in the source but no record in the artifact, because every row was refused — for this source, because their coordinates are written the wrong way round. Disjoint from states_absent and from states_covered.

organization.description: Null, not a guess. The source file names no publishing organisation anywhere.

licence.description: Null, not a guess. No licence accompanied the data.

snapshot_declared_version.description: Null, not a guess. The source declares no dataset version.

snapshot_last_updated_at.description: The newest record-level updated_at in the source: its own audit timestamp, zone undeclared, so no zone suffix is claimed.

records_moved_or_exchanged.description: Pinned. The instrument refuses; it never corrects.

type_vocabulary.description: The closed vocabulary a Product mapping decision would map INTO. Declared, not applied: every record's type is null.

facility_id.description: Stable identity, derived from the source's own unique row id. Distinct in shape from facilities 1.1's ng_<state>_<n> ids so the two lineages can never be confused for one another.

name.description: NFC-normalised, control characters stripped, whitespace collapsed. Casing is carried as the source has it: re-casing corrupts acronyms, so it is a consumer display concern.

type.description: Null on every record, deliberately. Mobile filters non-emergency results by type against {hospital, clinic, health_centre, pharmacy}; this source has no such column, only facility_level, which is a tier of care rather than a kind of facility. The mapping is a Product decision because it determines which facilities a user is shown for self-care versus urgent care. The vocabulary a decision would map into is declared in _metadata.unresolved_fields.type_vocabulary.

city_area.description: The LGA name. facilities 1.1 populated this field with a mixture of LGA names and free text, so an LGA is consistent with its dominant existing use, not a change of meaning.

latitude.description: Non-null on every record. Rows without a usable pair are quarantined.

longitude.description: Non-null on every record. Rows without a usable pair are quarantined.

phone.description: E.164, normalised from the source and never invented. Null when the source value was absent, malformed or a placeholder. Public-use intent is NOT established; see the provenance record.

opening_hours.description: Mapped only from the source's clean enum values; the free-text tail becomes null and is listed in _metadata.unmapped_source_values.

emergency_capable.description: Null on every record. facilities 1.1 derived this from type == 'hospital'; this source has no type, and none of its 90 columns records emergency capability.

services.description: Each key is read from exactly one source Yes/No column (tools/facilities/mappings.py SERVICES_SOURCE_COLUMNS); no other capability exists. Null means the source said neither Yes nor No. It is never coerced to false: 'we do not know whether this clinic has an ambulance' and 'this clinic has no ambulance' are different statements, and only one of them is safe to show a user.

lga_id.description: The source's own id, scoped to the LGA NAME rather than the state: six homonymous LGA names carry one id in two states each. Key an LGA by (state, city_area); never by lga_id alone.

source_updated_at.description: The source's record-level audit timestamp, zone undeclared.

source_record.description: Identity and provenance only. Every original value stays recoverable by joining source_id against the committed, hash-pinned source CSV. The administrative ids are the source's own and each maps to exactly one name.
